publisher.source: separate ephemeral CI test publisher keypair
publisher.publisherPublicKey: pinned at child process launch via allowlisted public-only environment, never supplied in DECIDE payload
publisher.canonicalization: domain-separated fixed positional JSON array, exact allowlist
publisher.policyDigest: SHA-256 of accepted W2.5 canonical synthetic bundle

pdpSigning.process: standalone Node child_process.spawn with fixed script, no shell and minimal allowlisted env
pdpSigning.trustedBootstrap: publisher public trust root pinned in child launch environment; PDP public key pinned from exact spawned local child
pdpSigning.evaluatedRules: the child verifies signed policy artifact and executes synthetic deny/allow rules itself
pdpSigning.uniqueRequestNonce: crypto.randomUUID generated by parent per child evaluation
pdpSigning.abort: AbortSignal kills child via SIGKILL, child close tracked

validates: policy digest, version, epoch and time window
independent child signer public key and signature
signed decision and synthetic rule semantics
W2.5 registry state after awaited child and again after W2.4 audit
no operational authorization and no actual data
verifier.failureBehavior: DENY before fake source for all signature, time, scope, audit and transport failures
verifier.publicResponse: only closed 403/503 via previously accepted W2.5 BFF interpreter
verifier.limits: local trusted child bootstrap, not an independent remote CA or attested binary

tests.executor: GitHub Actions exact Draft PR head, no Docker/Postgres/OCI
attackCases: policy body edit or extra field
child rejects correctly signed policy if launched with different publisher public root
separate process actually executes fake rule and signs DENY
modified decision, signature or signing key
revocation, policy replacement and expiry while PDP response pending
no child orphan and no secret persistence

limitations: PDP signing key is not externally authenticated by a certificate authority or pinned long-term identity: startup trust relies on launching a known local ephemeral child and trusting its first public key over a local pipe.
The publisher and PDP signing keys are temporary, have no HSM, secure rotation, PKI, revocation distribution or certified custody.
The decision evaluates only synthetic rules in a CI Node PDP, not official production business authorization and not the previous Python W1 simulator.
An injected synthetic test clock is used for policy validity, not an independently trusted distributed time authority or trusted timestamp.
W2.5 policy authority is single-process, not globally consistent across production instances or outages.
W2.4 file-backed hash chain and W2.5 version trace remain test-only, with no durable independently anchored signed audit or retention policy.
No official source authority, real shareholders, real trade/payment/accounting, SQL instrumentation, production route registration, database or Docker.
A valid local signature proves key possession and message integrity under the trusted local bootstrap assumptions; it does not attest the operating system, executable build or absence of compromise.
